findings.title: Operator dashboard measures personal analysis activity, not review workload
findings.observation: The dashboard uses owned history and the owner-scoped summary endpoint. Review counts are a separate queue resource. This is valid personal activity reporting, but it does not answer how many farmer submissions need attention.
findings.recommendation: Add a Review overview with pending cases, oldest submitted age, information requests, reviewed this period and unavailable/partial evidence. Keep My analyses as a separately named scope.
findings.acceptance: An operator with zero personal analyses and several pending farmer submissions sees the pending workload accurately.

findings.title: Planner queue still calls a model score SUITABILITY
findings.observation: The queue card reads compatibility_pct directly and labels it SUITABILITY. New shared detail sections call ranking values model scores, so the two views still disagree.
findings.recommendation: Use Model score only where a valid scored crop result exists. Show preliminary/unassessed explicitly and keep review decisions in a separate badge.
findings.acceptance: The same session has consistent score meaning in inbox, detail, map and export; a missing score remains unassessed.

findings.title: Heatmap color semantics use local min/max for every displayed layer
findings.observation: The review heatColor function scales each layer by the values in that record and maps higher relative values to green. Equal values use t=.75, also producing green. This displays relative magnitude, not a demonstrated favorable condition.
findings.recommendation: Give each non-soil layer its own units and numerical legend. Use a neutral sequential palette for measured magnitude and a separately documented assessment palette only when a valid grading rule exists. Preserve missing cells. NPK and soil pH remain outside this work.
findings.acceptance: A uniform-value grid cannot imply universally favorable conditions. Different parcels using a shared legend remain comparable.

findings.title: Legacy fallback text infers limited vegetation/non-arable surface from any NDVI value
findings.observation: When the non-crop fallback has any numeric NDVI and no explanation bullets, it inserts the same limited-vegetation/non-arable wording without inspecting the NDVI magnitude or why the result is incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Show the recorded value, its period and available coverage. Explain the actual reason a crop result is unavailable. Keep land-use or field confirmation separate.
findings.acceptance: A partial result with a positive numeric NDVI does not receive a conclusion triggered only by the presence of that number.

findings.title: Rejection reason is required by the UI but not by the review API
findings.observation: The dialog requires a nonempty rejection note. VerifySessionBody accepts optional notes, and the endpoint/database decision path does not enforce the same note requirement. The existing pending-only database update is a useful safety guard.
findings.recommendation: Enforce decision reason and note constraints server-side, matching the UI maximum. Return an explicit conflict for an already-decided case and preserve the first decision.
findings.acceptance: A direct authenticated API rejection with a blank note is refused. Two reviewers cannot overwrite one another; the second sees the current decision.

findings.title: No explicit information-request and revision-linked resubmission flow
findings.observation: The inspected review endpoint offers verified/rejected. Reposting an already rejected session returns its existing decision rather than reopening it. Retaining decisions is correct, but there is no explicit needs-information case lifecycle in these endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Add Request information with required correction items, a farmer response and a linked new revision. Preserve the reviewed analysis snapshot and decision history.
findings.acceptance: A farmer can address a requested correction and submit a new linked revision without erasing the previous reviewer decision.

findings.title: Review inbox pagination still downloads all pages first
findings.observation: The server supports bounded queue pages and q search, but getPlannerQueue calls the shared _pagedList loop until has_more is false. The screen then searches and paginates the complete loaded list. Queue responses also include heavy snapshot/grid detail.
findings.recommendation: Reuse a bounded query controller for queue status/search/page. Request lightweight listing fields and load full snapshot/grid only through the existing detail endpoint.
findings.acceptance: Opening 500 controlled submissions fetches one listing page, searching reaches the server, and opening one case fetches its full detail.

findings.title: Map and inbox share mutable queue/filter state without a query generation guard
findings.observation: Opening Map Analysis requests status=all through loadPlannerQueue, which changes the same plannerQueueStatus and rows used by the inbox. Competing status/search requests are not guarded by a queue generation token.
findings.recommendation: Separate PlanningMapController and ReviewQueueController. Guard responses by owner, filter and request generation; visiting the map must not change inbox filters.
findings.acceptance: Pending -> map -> inbox preserves the selected inbox filter. Delayed older filter responses cannot replace the current view.

findings.title: Queue failure and search-no-match states remain ambiguous
findings.observation: The empty branch checks the unfiltered queue rather than the searched result. Initial fetch failures can end at No submissions found after a transient snackbar; count failures are swallowed and zero/stale values have no clear state.
findings.recommendation: Persist resource errors, retain labeled stale data, offer retry, and separate loading/valid empty/no-match/error. Counters need independent loading/error states.
findings.acceptance: Searching a nonempty queue with no matching name shows No matching submissions. An HTTP failure never certifies an empty workload or a zero count.

findings.title: Review detail loading and URL reentry need a coherent route lifecycle
findings.observation: Detail is awaited before opening the dialog, so a slow fetch has no immediate detail loading view. The linked-record guard retains _openedRecord and skips the same ID on reentry; route Back/Forward, retry and dialog close need explicit regression coverage. These browser scenarios were not reproduced in this review.
findings.recommendation: Use a full-page review route with a loading/error/retry state keyed to the case/revision ID. Preserve inbox filters and scroll on return. Keep a small confirmation dialog only for the final decision.
findings.acceptance: A direct link, refresh, failed-load retry and Back/Forward can reopen the same case reliably; repeated clicks cannot stack stale record dialogs.

findings.title: Queue and detail retain rigid desktop layouts
findings.observation: Queue cards always use two columns; filter controls and KPI/header rows are ordinary Rows. The review dialog also contains fixed-height two-column sections. This is a source-observed overflow risk, not a newly reproduced device failure.
findings.recommendation: Use adaptive table/cards, wrapping filters, a collapsible map and a full-page detail layout at narrow/zoomed widths. Keep the decision action accessible while scrolling evidence.
findings.acceptance: Test 480x700, 1000x500 and 1280x900 plus 200% browser zoom on inbox and full review, with no unreachable actions.

findings.title: Planning-map summary mixes record scope and fixed overlay readiness
findings.observation: The map merges loaded owned history and submitted farmer analyses, includes a useful loaded-record badge, but its summary says Total Analyzed Lands/Across all saved analyses and Infrastructure Overlays Ready unconditionally. This is not a complete Panabo land inventory.
findings.recommendation: Label the dataset, filters, record count, distinct farm count and last refresh. Derive overlay availability from actual record/capability state and keep missing coverage visible.
findings.acceptance: An unavailable overlay is not labeled Ready. A displayed count is identified as records or distinct farms, with the exact authorized scope.

findings.title: Existing snapshot/version data needs visible review context
findings.observation: Sessions already store result snapshots, farm/boundary versions and review timestamps. The inspected review UI does not provide a clear version-comparison header/timeline. The farm boundary_version currently increments even for metadata edits, so a simple version mismatch must not automatically claim geometry changed.
findings.recommendation: Show the analyzed geometry/version/date, current geometry fingerprint where available, and decision timeline. Distinguish a geometry change from a rename or archive action.
findings.acceptance: A historical review remains tied to its original analysis; a farm rename does not falsely label the boundary as changed.

findings.title: Inbox ordering and cards emphasize analysis date instead of waiting time
findings.observation: The queue is ordered by analyzed_at descending and cards display the analysis date. submitted_at exists, but the default queue does not prioritize elapsed review waiting time.
findings.recommendation: Default Pending to oldest submitted first, offer explicit sort, and display submitted date plus waiting age. Add lightweight follow-up tasks or assignments only when operationally needed.
findings.acceptance: An older pending submission can be found first even when its underlying analysis is older than a newly submitted case.
